title: Direct Interface Mode Overview

children: What is the Direct Interface Mode?

A direct interface involves the system writing the data directly to/from 
 a database table. Using this method to download, the ERP first places 
 data in a temporary "transfer" database table. When the interface 
 process is initiated, the system retrieves the data from this "transfer" 
 download table and places it into the appropriate SCALE database table (such 
 as the shipment header table). The purpose of these transfer tables is 
 to preserve the integrity of the system database tables.

Using this method to upload, when the interface process is initiated, 
 SCALE places data that is eligible for uploading into a "transfer" 
 upload table. This eligible data has reached a minimum user-defined status, 
 such as "load confirmed" for shipments or "closed" 
 for receipt containers. The ERP then will retrieve this data and insert 
 it into its database.
When are Direct Interfaces Commonly Used?

You would typically use the direct method 
 if you want to write directly to an interface database table. Generally, 
 this method is appealing if want to have data seamlessly upload/download 
 to the database, without having to configure and maintain such things 
 as data maps or XML style sheets.
What Actions can a Direct Interface Perform?

SCALE direct interface mode supports four data actions (for uploads and 
 downloads):

: 
 This action allows you to introduce new records to the system (downloads), 
 or provide data to the ERP (uploads). Generally, this is the action you 
 would perform using the interface.

In direct mode, suppose your ERP generates data that is ready to be 
 imported into the system. When the interface is started, this "new" 
 data is imported into the SCALE database. This data then can be processed 
 by the user.

: 
 This action allows you to update records that were interfaced to the system 
 from the ERP. Generally, records can be changed until they reach a certain 
 processing point in the system. As a rule, change verification of interfaced 
 records follows the same standards as the change action within the system. 
 For example, you cannot change the carrier on a shipment once it's been 
 ship confirmed; therefore, you cannot change the carrier on a ship-confirmed 
 shipment via the interface. To determine when a change action is prohibited, 
 please review the help and check your own processing rules for the functional 
 area in question. Change actions can be used for downloads only.

In direct mode, suppose your ERP generates data that is meant to update 
 records that already exist in the system. When the interface is started, 
 this "change" data is processed by the system and interfaced 
 into the SCALE database. The changes to records, then, are merged into the 
 SCALE database (which houses the existing data records).

: 
 This action allows you to remove records from the system that were interfaced 
 from the ERP. Like the Change action, you can delete a record until it 
 reaches a certain processing point in the system. The information provided 
 for the Change action above also applies for the Delete action. Delete 
 actions can be used for downloads only.

In direct mode, suppose your ERP generates data representing already-existing 
 records that need to be deleted from the SCALE database. When the interface 
 is started, this "delete" data is processed by the system and 
 interfaced into the SCALE database. The system then deletes the appropriate 
 data from the database. For example, suppose there is an order that was 
 canceled, the ERP would then send down data identifying this order. The 
 system would then interface this data in, and make the appropriate deletion 
 from the database.

: 
 This action allows you to update a current record (that the system sees 
 is a duplicate), rather than create a second record with the updated information. 
 If no matching record is found, the system will insert a new record. This 
 is helpful if your ERP system generates data that does not indicate that 
 it is new data or changed data. Save actions can be used for downloads 
 and uploads.

In direct mode, suppose your ERP generates data representing either 
 new or already-existing records that need to be added/changed from the 
 SCALE database. When the interface is started, this "save" data 
 is processed by the system and interfaced into the SCALE database, depending 
 on the status of the data in the system. If the data already exists, the 
 system will handle this data record as a Change action. If the data does 
 not exist, the system will handle this as a New action.

What are the Basic Steps to Implement / Use a 
 Direct Interface?

The following configurations need to be addressed to process data via 
 a direct interface:

First, you need to create an interface 
 process record, which determines how data will be downloaded/uploaded 
 between the system and the ERP. Each functional area has its own process 
 settings for the interface. For example, in the Receiving process record, 
 there is a separate detail record for each interface process you want 
 to use (such as "receiving direct upload," "receiving XML 
 download," etc).

Next, you will need to address the various interface system values. These values 
 mostly involve technical decisions that you have to address in order for 
 the system to run your interface properly, such as in what status you 
 want data to be eligible for uploading, or directories you want delimited 
 files to be downloaded from.

Finally, you will need to decide if you want to 
 run your interface manually, 
 or have the system kick it off       automatically 
 during scheduled time(s) of the day. If you decide to run it automatically, 
 you need to define a job record in the Scheduled Job Window.

How Does the System Know Which Data to Download 
 to SCALE?

The system will attempt to process any data that resides in the appropriate 
 download database table.
 Your ERP will have to be configured to place data in these tables.

How Does the System Know Which Data to Upload 
 to the ERP?

The system will attempt to upload data that has attained a certain 
 status:

, you can define what data is uploaded per status on the Functional Area Window. You can also use an upload criteria record to further define what shipment data is uploaded for a certain status. For example, 
 you could define the statuses "Load Confirm Pending" and "Closed" to include in interface uploads. When an eligible shipment's trailing status meets this status, then the system will write a record in the upload order table.
, you can define what data is uploaded using a global setting in the Interface System Values Window.
Where Does Data Go When Downloaded into SCALE?

The answer for this depends on what type of data you are interfacing 
 into the system. For example, you could have downloaded orders to go into 
 the pool (in the Planned Shipment Insight screen), or as an "unassigned shipment" 
 (in the Shipment Insight screen). These statuses can be configured in the Interface 
 System Values Window.
